# jev-planner

> A CLI, and the library behind it, that writes a coding plan with two agents
> and a judge. Codex and Claude Code each draft a plan for the same task in the
> repository, review each other's draft, and Jev — TypeSafe's typed judge —
> picks the stronger plan and the agent that writes the final version. Every
> agent runs read-only. Node >= 20.19. MIT. Ships ESM and CommonJS with type
> declarations.

## Install

    npm install -g jev-planner

or, without installing, `npx jev-planner "<coding task>"`. It needs the
`codex` and `claude` CLIs installed and logged in, and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` set
for Jev. `jev-planner doctor` checks all three.

## Minimal working example

```sh
jev-planner doctor
jev-planner "Add rate limiting to the public API" -o PLAN.md
```

The plan goes to stdout, or to the file given with `-o`; progress goes to
stderr. `--json` prints `{ plan, verdict, finalizer }` instead.

The same flow from code:

```ts
import { ClaudeAgent, CodexAgent, Planner, TypeSafeJevJudge } from 'jev-planner'

const planner = new Planner(new CodexAgent(), new ClaudeAgent(), new TypeSafeJevJudge())
const { plan, verdict, finalizer } = await planner.plan({
  task: 'Add rate limiting to the public API',
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  timeoutMs: 600_000,
})
```

## API

| Export                | Kind     | What it does                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Planner`             | class    | `new Planner(codex, claude, jev).plan(options)`: drafts, cross-reviews, finalizes            |
| `CodexAgent`          | class    | A `PlanningAgent` that runs `codex exec` in a read-only sandbox                              |
| `ClaudeAgent`         | class    | A `PlanningAgent` that runs `claude -p` in plan mode                                         |
| `TypeSafeJevJudge`    | class    | A `JevJudge` backed by `@typesafe-ai/sdk`; reads `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`                          |
| `runDoctor`           | function | `runDoctor(cwd)` checks the CLIs, the API key and the directory                              |
| `ProcessError`        | class    | Thrown when an agent CLI exits non-zero, is killed, or times out                             |
| `TaskValidationError` | class    | Thrown by `plan` before any call when the task is empty or a placeholder                     |
| `ProcessResult`       | type     | `{ stdout, stderr }` of a finished agent process                                             |
| `CheckResult`         | type     | `{ name, ok, detail }`, one `runDoctor` check                                                |
| `AgentName`           | type     | `'codex' \| 'claude'`                                                                        |
| `AgentRequest`        | type     | `{ prompt, cwd, timeoutMs }`, what a `PlanningAgent` is given                                |
| `PlanningAgent`       | type     | `{ name, generate(request) }`, the agent interface `Planner` drives                          |
| `JevJudge`            | type     | `{ judge({ task, codexPlan, claudePlan, model? }) }`, returns a `JevVerdict`                 |
| `JevVerdict`          | type     | Scores and confidences for both plans, and the chosen finalizer                              |
| `PlanOptions`         | type     | `{ task, cwd, timeoutMs, maxReviewRounds?, jevModel?, finalizer?, allowAnyTask?, onStage? }` |
| `PlanResult`          | type     | `{ plan, verdict, finalizer, drafts: { codex, claude } }`                                    |

## Mistakes to avoid

- **Treating a run as free.** One plan is 5 or 7 agent calls and 1 or 2 Jev
  calls, each billed to the account it runs under. Run `jev-planner doctor`
  first rather than a real task to check the setup.
- **Sending a template as the task.** A placeholder — `TODO`, `<coding task>`,
  `{{task}}`, text with no letters — is rejected with `TaskValidationError`
  before any billed call. Pass `--allow-any-task` (`allowAnyTask: true` in the
  API) only when that text really is the task.
- **Giving the task two ways.** The task comes from the arguments, from `-f`,
  or from stdin — passing both arguments and `-f` is an error.
- **Expecting the agents to edit code.** Both run read-only; the output is a
  plan, not a change.
- **A short `--timeout`.** It applies to each agent call, not the whole run,
  and defaults to 600 seconds; a large repository needs most of it.
